Cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, also known as reperfusion syndrome, is a dysregulated state of cerebral blood flow following the restoration of arterial blood flow to the brain, usually following treatment of [carotid artery stenosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carotid_artery_stenosis).
cerebral laceration is a type of [traumatic brain injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traumatic_brain_injury) that occurs when the tissue of the brain is mechanically cut or torn.
cerebral organoid describes an artificially grown, [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro), tissue resembling parts of the human [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain).

Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) is the net [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure) gradient causing [cerebral blood flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_blood_flow) to the brain (brain [perfusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfusion)).

Cerebral diplopia or polyopia describes seeing two or more images arranged in ordered rows, columns, or diagonals after [fixation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixation_(visual)) on a [stimulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(psychology)).

definition: Cerebral vasospasm is the prolonged, intense [vasoconstriction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasoconstriction) of the larger [conducting arteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conducting_artery) in the [subarachnoid space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subarachnoid_space) which is initially surrounded by a [clot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clot).

Cerebritis is the [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation) of the [cerebrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrum), which performs a number of important functions, such as memory and speech.

cerebroprotectant (formerly known as a neuroprotectant) is a [drug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug) that is intended to protect the brain after the onset of acute [ischemic stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ischemic_stroke).

Cerebrospinal fluid diversion is a procedure that is used to drain fluid from the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord).

cerebrospinal fluid leak (CSF leak or CSFL) is a medical condition where the [cerebrospinal fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrospinal_fluid) (CSF) that surrounds the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord) leaks out of one or more holes or tears in the [dura mater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dura_mater).

cerebrospinal venous system (CSVS) consists of the interconnected venous systems of the brain (the [cerebral venous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_circulation)) and the spine (the [vertebral venous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batson_venous_plexus)).

definition: nerve guidance conduit (also referred to as an artificial nerve conduit or artificial nerve graft, as opposed to an [autograft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autograft)) is an artificial means of guiding axonal regrowth to facilitate [nerve regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve_regeneration) and is one of several clinical treatments for [nerve injuries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve_injury).
Nerve injury is an [injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury) to a [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve).

nerve net consists of interconnected [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s lacking a [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) or any form of [cephalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalization).
nerve plexus is a [plexus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plexus) (branching network) of intersecting [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve)s.
nerve root () is the initial segment of a [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve) leaving the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system).

nerve sheath tumor is a type of [tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor) of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) ([nervous system neoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system_neoplasm)) which is made up primarily of the [myelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myelin) surrounding [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve)s.
nerve tissue protein is a biological molecule related to the function and maintenance of normal [nervous tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_tissue).
nerve to the stapedius is a branch of the [facial nerve (CN VII)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_nerve) which innervates the [stapedius muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stapedius_muscle).

nerve tract is a bundle of nerve fibers ([axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon)s) connecting [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleus_(neuroanatomy)) of the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system).

definition: nervous system is the [highly complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_system) part of an [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) that coordinates its [actions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior) and [sensory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense) [information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information) by transmitting [signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_potential) to and from different parts of its body.

Nervous system diseases, also known as nervous system or neurological disorders, refers to a small class of [medical condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_condition)s affecting the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).

nervous system tumor is a [tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor) that arises within the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system), either the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (CNS) or the [peripheral nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral_nervous_system) (PNS).

NEST is a [simulation software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulation_software) for [spiking neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiking_neural_network) models, including large-scale neuronal networks.

Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN) (Dutch: Nederlands Herseninstituut) is a research institute of the [Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Netherlands_Academy_of_Arts_and_Sciences) (KNAW) that carries out [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) research with special emphasis on the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and [visual system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_system).
categories: Neuroscience research centers in the Netherlands

definition: Network neuroscience is an approach to understanding the structure and function of the [human brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) through an approach of [network science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_science), through the [paradigm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradigm) of [graph theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_theory).

Neural accommodation or neuronal accommodation occurs when a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron) or [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle) cell is depolarised by slowly rising current ([ramp depolarisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramp_function)) in vitro.

Neural adaptation or sensory adaptation is a gradual decrease over time in the responsiveness of the [sensory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_system) to a constant [stimulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)).

Neural backpropagation is the phenomenon in which, after the [action potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_potential) of a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron) creates a voltage spike down the [axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon) (normal propagation), another impulse is generated from the [soma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soma_(biology)) and propagates towards the [apical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apical_dendrite) portions of the dendritic arbor or [dendrites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dendrites) (from which much of the original input current originated).
Neural circuit reconstruction is the reconstruction of the detailed circuitry of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) (or a portion of the nervous system) of an animal.
Neural cliques are network-level [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory) coding units in the [hippocampus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippocampus).

Neural coding (or neural representation) refers to the relationship between a [stimulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)) and its respective neuronal responses, and the [signalling relationships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrophysiology) among networks of neurons in an [ensemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuronal_ensemble).
Neural computation is the [information processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_processing_(psychology)) performed by networks of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s.

Neural Computation is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [neural computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_computation), including modeling the brain and the design and construction of neurally-inspired information processing systems.

neural crest is a ridge-like structure that is formed transiently between the [epidermal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermal) [ectoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectoderm) and [neural plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_plate) during [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) development.

Neural decoding is a [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) field concerned with the hypothetical reconstruction of sensory and other stimuli from information that has already been encoded and represented in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) by [networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_neural_network) of [neurons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurons).

Neural dust is a theoretical class of nanometer-sized devices operated as [wirelessly powered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_power_transfer) nerve sensors; it would be a type of [brain–computer interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain–computer_interface).

Neural facilitation, also known as paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), is a phenomenon in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) in which postsynaptic potentials (PSPs) ([EPPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End-plate_potential), [EPSPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excitatory_postsynaptic_potential) or [IPSPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhibitory_postsynaptic_potential)) evoked by an impulse are increased when that impulse closely follows a prior impulse.

neural fold is a structure that arises during [neurulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurulation) in the embryonic development of both [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s and [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s among other organisms.

neural groove is a shallow median groove of the [neural plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_plate) between the [neural folds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_folds) of an [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo).

Neural Impulse Actuator (NIA) is a [brain–computer interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain–computer_interface) (BCI) device developed by [OCZ Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OCZ_Technology).

neural network (NN) or neural net, is a [computational model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_model) inspired by the structure and functions of [biological neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_neural_networks).

neural network, also called a neuronal network, is an interconnected population of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s (typically containing multiple [neural circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_circuit)s).

neural pathway is the connection formed by [axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon)s that project from [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s to make [synapse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synapse)s onto neurons in another location, to enable [neurotransmission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurotransmission) (the sending of a signal from one region of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) to another).

Neural Plasticity is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering all aspects of [neuroplasticity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroplasticity), especially when concerning its functional involvement in the regulation of behavior and in [psychopathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychopathology).

definition: Neural Regeneration Research is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on [neuroregeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroregeneration) and [stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cell)s.

neural substrate is a term used in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to indicate the part of the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (i.e., [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord)) that underlies a specific [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior), [cognitive process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_process), or [psychological state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_state).
Neural synchrony is the correlation of [brain activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_activity) across two or more people over time.
Neural tissue engineering is a specific sub-field of [tissue engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_engineering).

neural tube is the [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)nic precursor to the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system), which is made up of the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) and [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord).

Neuro-oncology is the study of [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_neoplasms) and [spinal cord neoplasms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_neoplasms), many of which are (at least eventually) very dangerous and life-threatening ([astrocytoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrocytoma), [glioma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glioma), [glioblastoma multiforme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glioblastoma_multiforme), [ependymoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ependymoma), [pontine glioma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontine_glioma), and brain stem tumors are among the many examples of these).

Neuro-ophthalmology is an academically-oriented [subspecialty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subspecialty) that merges the fields of [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology) and [ophthalmology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ophthalmology), often dealing with complex systemic diseases that have manifestations in the [visual system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_system).

Neuroacanthocytosis is a label applied to several genetic neurological conditions in which the blood contains misshapen, spiculated [red blood cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erythrocyte) called [acanthocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acanthocytes).

definition: Neuroanatomy is a branch of [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) and [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) that studies the structure and organization of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).
Neuroanthropology is the study of the relationship between culture and the brain.{{efn | Daniel Lende and Greg Downey recount the origins of a definition of .

Neuroarchaeology is a sub-discipline of [archaeology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeology) that uses neuroscientific data to infer things about [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) form and function in human cognitive evolution.

Neurobiology of Aging is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) monthly [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier).

Neurobiology of Disease is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on disease mechanisms underlying disorders of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) and [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychopathology).

Neurobiology of Stress is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on the [neurobiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurobiology) of [stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_(biology)).

Neurocardiology is the study of the [neurophysiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurophysiological), [neurological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology) and [neuroanatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroanatomy) aspects of [cardiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiology), including the neurological origins of cardiac disorders.

Neurocase is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) journal specializing in case studies in the [neuropsychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuropsychology), [neuropsychiatry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuropsychiatry) and [behavioral neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral_neurology) of adults and children.

Neurochemical Research is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering [neurochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurochemistry).

neurochip is an [integrated circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_circuit) chip (such as a [microprocessor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microprocessor)) that is designed for interaction with [neuronal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuronal) cells.

Neurocinema or neurocinematics is the science of how watching movies, or particular scenes from movies affect human [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain)s, and the response the human brain gives to any given movie or scene.

Neurocognitive functions are [cognitive function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_function)s closely linked to the integrity of specific [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) systems—particular [cortical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_cortex) and subcortical regions, [neural pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_pathway)s, and large-scale networks—such that disruption of those neural substrates produces characteristic patterns of cognitive impairment.

Neurocomputational speech processing is computer-simulation of [speech production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_production) and [speech perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_perception) by referring to the natural neuronal processes of [speech production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_production) and [speech perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_perception), as they occur in the human [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) ([central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) and [peripheral nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral_nervous_system)).

Neurocomputing is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research on [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence), [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning), and [neural computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_computation).

Neurocriminology is an emerging sub-discipline of [biocriminology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biocriminology) and [criminology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminology) that applies [brain imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_imaging) techniques and principles from [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to understand, predict, and prevent crime.

Neurocristopathy is a diverse class of pathologies that may arise from defects in the development of tissues containing cells commonly derived from the embryonic [neural crest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_crest) cell lineage.

Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation is a heterogenous group of inherited [neurodegenerative disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurodegenerative_disease)s, still under research, in which iron accumulates in the [basal ganglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basal_ganglia), either resulting in progressive [dystonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dystonia), [parkinsonism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkinsonism), [spasticity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spasticity), [optic atrophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optic_atrophy), [retinal degeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinopathy), [neuropsychiatric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuropsychiatric), or diverse neurologic abnormalities.
related: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke

definition: Neurodevelopmental framework for learning, like all frameworks, is an organizing structure through which learners and learning can be understood.
Neuroectoderm (or neural ectoderm or neural tube epithelium) consists of cells derived from the [ectoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectoderm).
neuroectodermal neoplasm is a [neoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasm) or [tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor) of the [neuroectoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroectoderm).
neuroeffector junction is a site where a motor neuron releases a neurotransmitter to affect a target—non-neuronal—cell.
Neuroelectrics is a [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona)-based Spanish company which produces devices to stimulate and treat the brain.

Neuroenhancement or cognitive enhancement is the experimental use of [pharmacological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmacological) or non-pharmacological methods intended to [improve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_enhancement) [cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) and [affective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affect_(psychology)) abilities in healthy people who don't have any [mental illness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_disorder).

Neuroepidemiology is a science of [incidence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incidence_(epidemiology)), [prevalence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prevalence), [risk factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_factor)s, [natural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history_of_disease) and [prognosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prognosis) of neurological disorders, as well as of experimental neuroepidemiology, which is research based on [clinical trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_trial)s of effectiveness or efficacy of various interventions in neurological disorders.

Neuroepigenetics is the study of how [epigenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenetic) changes to [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) affect the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).
Neuroergonomics is the application of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to [ergonomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ergonomics).

Neuroethics is a triannual [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [academic journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal) covering the field of [neuroethics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroethics) and related issues in the sciences of the mind.

Neuroethics Research Unit was created in 2006, at the [[:fr:Institut de recherches cliniques de Montréal|Institut de recherches cliniques de Montréal]] (IRCM), which is affiliated to the [Université de Montréal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Université_de_Montréal).

Neurogaming is a nascent form of [gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_gaming) that involves the use of [brain–computer interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain–computer_interface)s such as [EEG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EEG) so that users can interact with the game without the need of traditional controllers.

Neurogastronomy is the study of [flavor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavor_(taste)) [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception) and the ways it affects [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) and [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory).

Neurogenesis is the process by which [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) cells, the [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s, are produced by [neural stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_stem_cell)s (NSCs).

Neurogenetics is a quarterly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering the field of [neurogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurogenetics).

neurogenic placode is an area of thickening of the [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) in the [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)nic head [ectoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectoderm) layer that gives rise to neurons and other structures of the [sensory nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_nervous_system).

Neurogliaform cells (NGF) are inhibitory ([GABAergic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma-Aminobutyric_acid)) [interneuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interneuron)s found in the [cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_cortex) and the [hippocampus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippocampus).

Neurogrid is a piece of [computer hardware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_hardware) that is designed specifically for [simulation of biological brains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_simulation).

Neurohistory is an [interdisciplinary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdisciplinary) approach to [history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History) that leverages advances in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to tell new kinds of stories about the past, but especially of [deep history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_history).

neurohormone is any [hormone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormone) produced and released by [neuroendocrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroendocrine_cell)s (also called neurosecretory cells) into the blood.
Neurohospitalist is a term used for [physician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physician)s interested in inpatient neurological care.

Neurohydrodynamics is a division of [neurophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurophysics) that focuses on the [hydrodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrodynamics) of the neurological system.
related: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke

definition: Neuroimmunology is a field combining [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience), the study of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system), and [immunology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunology), the study of the [immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_system).
Neuroinflammation is [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation) of the [nervous tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_tissue).
Neuroinformatics is the emergent field that combines [informatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Informatics) and [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience).

Neurocritical care (or neurointensive care) is a medical field that treats life-threatening diseases of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) and identifies, prevents, and treats [secondary brain injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_brain_injury).

media.file: Iron Lung ward-Rancho Los Amigos Hospital GettyImages-515505698.jpg

definition: Neurolaw is a field of interdisciplinary study that explores the effects of discoveries in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) on legal rules and standards.

Neurologic Clinics is a [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) that covers [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology)-related topics, such as [multiple sclerosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_sclerosis), [epilepsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epilepsy), [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroke), [headache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headache), [sleep disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep_disorder)s, pediatric-specific neurology etc.

neurological examination is the assessment of [sensory neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_neuron) and [motor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_neuron) responses, especially [reflex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflex)es, to determine whether the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) is impaired.

Neurological reparative therapy (NRT) is a new model of treatment synthesized from a compilation of literature and research on how to better the lives of individuals who have a wide range of [mental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mind), [emotional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional), and [behavioral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral) disturbances – particularly children and adolescents.
Neurological Society of India (NSI) is the apex body representing neuroscientists of the country.

related: American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology
American Osteopathic Board of Neurology and Psychiatry

definition: Neurology is a weekly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) covering research in [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology).

Neurology India is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) published by [Medknow Publications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medknow_Publications) on behalf of the [Neurological Society of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurological_Society_of_India).

Neurology International is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) scientific journal covering research in the field of [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology), including clinical and experimental studies.
neuroma (; plural: neuromata or neuromas) is a growth or [tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor) of [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve) tissue.

Research, Innovation, and Dissemination Center for Neuromathematics (RIDC NeuroMat, or simply NeuroMat) is a Brazilian research center established in 2013 at the [Institute of Mathematics and Statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Mathematics_and_Statistics,_University_of_São_Paulo) in the [University of São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_São_Paulo) that is dedicated to integrating [mathematical modeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_modeling) and [theoretical neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_neuroscience).

Neuromechanics is an interdisciplinary field that combines [biomechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomechanics) and [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) to understand how the nervous system interacts with the skeletal and muscular systems to enable animals to move.

Neuromeres are distinct groups of [neural crest cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_crest_cell)s, forming segments in the [neural tube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_tube) of the early [embryonic development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_development) of the brain.

media.file: The Prosomeric Model of the vertebrate central nervous system.jpg
Schemata illustrating embryonic (a) and adult (b) location and abbreviations for neuromeres within the prosomeric model.png

definition: neurometric function is a mathematical formula relating the activity of brain cells to aspects of an animal's sensory experience or motor behavior.
Neurometrics is the science of measuring the underlying organization of the brain's electrical activity.

Neuromodulation: Technology at the Neural Interface is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) covering clinical, translational, and basic science research in the field of [neuromodulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuromodulation_(medicine)).

NeuroMolecular Medicine is a quarterly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) covering research on the molecular and biochemical basis of [neurological disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurological_disorder)s.

Neuromorality is an emerging field of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) that studies the connection between [morality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morality) and neuronal function.
Neuromorphic computing is a computing approach inspired by the human brain's structure and function.

Neuromorphic olfaction systems are bio-inspired computational architectures that mimic the neural processing mechanisms of biological olfactory systems using [neuromorphic engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuromorphic_engineering) principles.
Neuromuscular diagnostic tests are medical tests performed to diagnose disorders of the [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle)s and [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve)s.

Neuromuscular Disorders is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare_journal) that focuses on [neuromuscular disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuromuscular_disease), including [muscular dystrophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscular_dystrophy), [spinal muscular atrophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_muscular_atrophy), and [myasthenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myasthenia_gravis).

Neuromuscular drugs are chemical agents that are used to alter the transmission of nerve impulses to muscles, causing effects such as temporary paralysis of targeted [skeletal muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal_muscle)s.
categories: Drugs acting on the nervous system

definition: Neuromuscular medicine is a subspecialty of [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology) and [physiatry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_medicine_and_rehabilitation) that focuses the diagnosis and management of [neuromuscular disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuromuscular_disease)s.

neuron doctrine is the concept that the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) is made up of discrete individual cells, a discovery due to decisive neuro-anatomical work of [Santiago Ramón y Cajal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Ramón_y_Cajal) and later presented by, among others, [[Heinrich Wilhelm Gottfried von Waldeyer-Hartz|H.

neuronal ensemble is a population of [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) (or [cultured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_culture) [neurons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurons)) involved in a particular [neural computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_computation).

Memory allocation is a process that determines which specific [synapses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synapses) and [neurons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurons) in a neural network will store a given memory.

Neuronal sprouting is any process where [neurite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurite) growth occurs, typically through modifications to [synapses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synapses) While neural sprouting can be a beneficial process for recovery from brain injury, it can also have negative effects in some cases.

Neuronal tracing, or neuron reconstruction is a technique used in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) and to determine the [pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_pathway) of the [neurite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurite)s or neuronal processes, the [axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon)s and [dendrite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dendrite)s, of a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron).

NeuronStudio was a non-commercial program created at [Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Icahn_School_of_Medicine_at_Mount_Sinai) by the Computational Neurobiology and Imaging Center.

Neuroparasitology is an interdisciplinary field of biology at the intersection of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) and [parasitology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitology).

Neuropathology is the study of [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease) of nervous system tissue, usually in the form of either small surgical [biopsies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopsy) or whole-body [autopsies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy).

Neuropathology and Applied Neurobiology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) in the field of [neuropathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuropathology).

Neuropharmacology is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) in the field of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience).

Neurophilosophy, or the philosophy of neuroscience, is the interdisciplinary study of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) and [philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy) that explores the relevance of [neuroscientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscientific) studies to the arguments traditionally categorized as [philosophy of mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_mind).

Neurophysics (or neurobiophysics) is the branch of [biophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysics) dealing with the development and use of physical methods to gain information about the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).
Neuropixels probes (or The data from this survey is openly available.

Neuroplastic or neuroplastic and reconstructive surgery is the surgical specialty involved in reconstruction or restoration of patients who undergo surgery of the central or peripheral nervous system.

Neuroplasticity, also known as neural plasticity or just plasticity, is the medium of [neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(biology)) in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) to change through [growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurogenesis) and reorganization.

Neuropoiesis is the process by which neural stem cells differentiate to form mature [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s, [astrocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrocyte)s, and [oligodendrocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligodendrocyte)s in the adult mammal.
Neuropolitics is a science which investigates the interplay between the brain and politics.
Neuroprotection refers to the relative preservation of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)al structure and/or function.

Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) covering research in [psychiatry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatry) and [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology).

Neuropsychiatry is a branch of [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine) that deals with [psychiatry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatry) as it relates to [neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology), in an effort to understand and attribute behavior to the interaction of [neurobiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurobiology) and [social psychological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_psychological) factors.

Neuropsychologia is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that focuses on [cognitive neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_neuroscience).

Neuropsychopharmacology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Nature Portfolio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature_Portfolio).

NeuroQuantology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [interdisciplinary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdisciplinarity) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) meant to cover the intersection of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) and [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Neurorehabilitation and Neural Repair is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) that publishes papers in the fields of [rehabilitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_medicine_and_rehabilitation) and [clinical neurology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_neurology).

Neurorobotics is the combined study of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience), [robotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotics), and [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence).

Neuroscience is the [scientific study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science) of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) (the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain), [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord), and [peripheral nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral_nervous_system)), its functions, and its disorders.

Neuroscience is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience).

Neuroscience and intelligence refers to the various [neurological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurological) factors that are partly responsible for the variation of [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence) within species or between different species.
related: List of animals by number of neurons

categories: International Behavioral Neuroscience Society academic journals

definition: Space neuroscience or astroneuroscience is the scientific study of the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (CNS) functions during [spaceflight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaceflight).

Neuroscience Letters is a biweekly rapid-publication [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) for short articles covering all aspects of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience).
Neuroscience nursing is a distinctive area within the discipline of [nursing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nursing).
neuroscience of aging is the study of the changes in the nervous system that occur with [aging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ageing).
neuroscience of music is the scientific study of brain-based mechanisms involved in the cognitive processes underlying [music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music).
neuroscience of rhythm refers to the various forms of rhythm generated by the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (CNS).
neuroscience of sex differences is the study of characteristics that separate brains of different sexes.

neuroscience of sleep is the study of the [neuroscientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) and [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) basis of the nature of [sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep) and its functions.
Neurosemiotics is an area of science which studies the neural aspects of meaning making.

Neurosexism is an alleged bias in the [neuroscience of sex differences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience_of_sex_differences) towards reinforcing harmful [gender stereotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_role).
neurosphere is a culture system composed of free-floating clusters of [neural stem cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_stem_cells).

Neurosyphilis is the infection of the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) by [Treponema pallidum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treponema_pallidum), the bacterium that causes the [sexually transmitted infection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexually_transmitted_infection) [syphilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syphilis).

Neurotherapeutics is a quarterly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) covering research on experimental treatments of [neurological disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurological_disorder)s.

Proximal diabetic neuropathy, also known as diabetic amyotrophy, is a complication of diabetes mellitus that affects the nerves that supply the thighs, hips, buttocks and/or lower legs.
